Calculate sample size to detect a prevalence above or below a threshold

Source: R/design_threshold.R
design_threshold.Rd

Design function: given a decision threshold and the true prevalence expected in the population, returns the number of people needed for test_threshold() (with its default exact binomial test) to show that the prevalence is above (or below) the threshold with the target power.

Three designs are supported:

No clustering (n_sites and n_per_site both NULL, default)

Returns the number of people.

Fixed number of people per site (n_per_site)

Solves for the number of sites needed.

Fixed number of sites (n_sites)

Solves for the number of people needed per site.

Usage

design_threshold(
  threshold,
  prevalence,
  power = 0.8,
  alternative = c("greater", "less", "two.sided"),
  sensitivity = 1,
  specificity = 1,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  n_sites = NULL,
  n_per_site = NULL,
  icc = 0
)

Arguments

threshold

Decision threshold for the true prevalence, strictly between 0 and 1 (for example 0.05 for the WHO pfhrp2/3 deletion threshold). This is the value test_threshold() tests against.

prevalence

The true prevalence expected in the population, in (0, 1). It must be above threshold for alternative = "greater" and below it for "less".

power

Target power, in (0, 1); default 0.80.

alternative

Which side of the threshold to look for, the same as in the test_threshold() call. "greater" (default) looks for a prevalence above the threshold, "less" for one below it, and "two.sided" for either.

sensitivity

Diagnostic sensitivity in (0, 1]; default 1 (the test never misses a case).

specificity

Diagnostic specificity in (0, 1]; default 1 (the test never gives a false positive). sensitivity + specificity must exceed 1.

conf_level

Confidence level, in (0, 1); default 0.95. The significance level of the test is 1 - conf_level.

n_sites

Optional whole number. Fixes the number of sites; the function solves for the number of people per site. Cannot be used with n_per_site.

n_per_site

Optional whole number. Fixes the number of people per site; the function solves for the number of sites. Cannot be used with n_sites.

icc

Intra-cluster correlation, in [0, 1]; default 0 (no clustering). An icc above 0 needs n_sites or n_per_site.

Value

A list with (every value NA, with a warning, if more than 100,000 people are needed without clustering):

n

Total number of people needed. With sites, n_sites * n_per_site.

n_sites

Number of sites (NULL with no clustering).

n_per_site

People per site (NULL with no clustering).

deff

Design effect of the returned design, 1 + (n_per_site - 1) * icc (1 with no clustering).

n_eff

Number of independent people needed: the exact answer with no clustering.

Details

Exact power. The power of a design is the chance that the exact binomial test in test_threshold() rejects when the true prevalence is prevalence. For \(n\) people and alternative = "greater", the test rejects when the number of positives \(X\) is at least the critical count \(k\), the smallest count with \(P(X \ge k \mid \theta_{app}) < \alpha\); the power is then \(P(X \ge k \mid p_{app})\). "less" is the mirror image, and "two.sided" adds the two tails, each at \(\alpha / 2\). This is worked out from the binomial distribution itself, not from a normal approximation, which can undersize the study badly at low prevalence.

Saw-tooth power and the choice of n. With an exact test, power does not always go up when people are added: counts are whole numbers, so the critical count jumps, and power goes up and down in a saw-tooth. For example, with threshold = 0.10, prevalence = 0.05, alternative = "less" and 95 percent confidence, 179 people give 81.3 percent power, 182 to 190 people all give less than 80 percent, and every number from 203 on gives at least 80 percent. The function returns the larger number (203): the smallest \(n\) from which every larger \(n\) also reaches the target power. This is the safe choice, as a few extra (or a few lost) people never drop the study below the target. Sample sizes up to 100,000 are checked. A design needing more than that without clustering (a prevalence very close to the threshold) gives a warning that reports the power 100,000 people would reach, and returns NA for every value.

Imperfect test. The test is worked out on the measured scale: a true prevalence \(p\) is measured as \(p_{app} = p \cdot Se + (1-p)(1-Sp)\), and the same for the threshold. The measured gap is the true gap times \(Se + Sp - 1\), so an imperfect test needs more people.

Clustering. The exact search above gives \(n_0\), the number of independent people needed (returned as n_eff). Clustering is then allowed for with the design effect, as in design_precision(): with n_per_site fixed, \(n = n_0 \cdot D_{eff}\) with \(D_{eff} = 1 + (n_{per site} - 1) ICC\); with n_sites fixed,

$$n = \frac{n_0 \cdot n_{sites} \cdot (1-ICC)}{n_{sites} - n_0 \cdot ICC}$$

which exists only when \(n_{sites} > n_0 \cdot ICC\) (each site is worth at most \(1/ICC\) independent people, however many are sampled there); otherwise the function stops. The number of sites (or people per site) is then rounded up, and n is n_sites * n_per_site. Scaling the exact unclustered answer by the design effect is an approximation: the effective sample size \(n / D_{eff}\) of the returned design is at least \(n_0\), but need not sit on the saw-tooth exactly where \(n_0\) does. The power assumes the analysis uses the same ICC.

References

MMS-SD Study Design Workshop. https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMS-SD_workshop/

Kish, L. (1965) Survey Sampling. Wiley. (Design effect.)

Rogan, W. J. & Gladen, B. (1978) Estimating prevalence from the results of a screening test. American Journal of Epidemiology 107(1), 71-76. doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.aje.a112510

See also

test_threshold

Examples

# Show that prevalence is above a 5 percent threshold when it is really
# 10 percent, with 80 percent power
design_threshold(threshold = 0.05, prevalence = 0.10)
#> $n
#> [1] 191
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 191
#> 

# Higher power needs more people
design_threshold(threshold = 0.05, prevalence = 0.10, power = 0.90)
#> $n
#> [1] 256
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 256
#> 

# Below the threshold instead
design_threshold(threshold = 0.10, prevalence = 0.05, alternative = "less")
#> $n
#> [1] 203
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> NULL
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> NULL
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 203
#> 

# Fixed number of people per site: how many sites?
design_threshold(threshold = 0.05, prevalence = 0.10,
                 n_per_site = 20, icc = 0.05)
#> $n
#> [1] 380
#> 
#> $n_sites
#> [1] 19
#> 
#> $n_per_site
#> [1] 20
#> 
#> $deff
#> [1] 1.95
#> 
#> $n_eff
#> [1] 191
#>
